tldr: Sleep-time compute allows LLMs to reason offline about contexts before queries arrive, reducing test-time compute by ~5× for the same accuracy or boosting accuracy by up to 13-18% when scaled.
contributions: Introduced sleep-time compute, which pre-computes inferences about contexts during model idle time
Created modified datasets Stateful GSM-Symbolic and Stateful AIME by splitting existing problems into context and question
Introduced Multi-Query GSM-Symbolic with multiple related queries per context
Demonstrated Pareto improvements in test-time compute vs. accuracy trade-offs
Showed amortization benefits reducing average cost per query by 2.5× across shared contexts
Provided analysis linking sleep-time compute efficacy to query predictability
methods: The authors modify two reasoning datasets (GSM-Symbolic and AIME) by splitting problems into context and question components, creating stateful testbeds. During sleep-time, an LLM is prompted to generate inferences about the context c, producing a re-represented context c'. At test-time, the model answers queries using a much smaller compute budget b << B given c'. They scale sleep-time compute via parallel generations for non-reasoning models and varying reasoning effort for models like o1 and o3-mini. For amortization analysis, they introduce Multi-Query GSM-Symbolic where a single context has multiple queries, generating additional Q&A pairs using o3-mini. They also analyze query predictability using log-probability under Llama2-70B base model.
results: Sleep-time compute reduces test-time compute needed for the same accuracy by ~5× on both Stateful GSM-Symbolic and Stateful AIME. Scaling sleep-time compute further increases accuracy by up to 13% on Stateful GSM-Symbolic and 18% on Stateful AIME. Amortizing across multiple queries reduces average cost per query by 2.5× with 10 queries per context. Sleep-time compute consistently outperforms pass@k parallel scaling at the same test-time token budget. The accuracy gap between sleep-time and standard test-time compute widens as questions become more predictable from context. 5 parallel sleep-time generations generally outperformed 10.
limitations: At high test-time compute budgets, standard test-time compute only slightly outperforms sleep-time compute, hypothesized because standard test-time only includes question-relevant content without distracting information
Diminishing returns from parallel sleep-time generations (5 outperformed 10)
Efficacy depends on query predictability from context — less effective for complex, unpredictable queries
